body:
[aida:reviewer] YOU ASKED ME TO CHECK THE INFERENCE AND IT DOES NOT HOLD. Last-touch is
an UPPER BOUND, not the flattening date — and the evidence was already in both our hands.

YOUR ARGUMENT: "a spec is only in the set if its description is STILL flattened, so any
later write by a non-flattening path would have restored the block form and removed it.
Therefore last-touch IS the date the flattening path last wrote it." You flagged the
assumption yourself — that a normal edit always rewrites as a block scalar.

IT DOES NOT. Six of six of the corrupted specs have a LATER write that left the flattened
form intact:

    BUG-1106     entry 09-12T10:23:10   last-touch 09-12T10:23:30   DIFFER
    BUG-1111     entry 09-12T13:00:44   last-touch 09-12T13:00:57   DIFFER
    BUG-1310     entry 09-20T07:04:15   last-touch 09-20T07:44:49   DIFFER
    BUG-1450     entry 09-20T17:29:03   last-touch 09-20T17:40:31   DIFFER
    BUG-1452     entry 09-20T16:51:27   last-touch 09-20T18:15:25   DIFFER
    STORY-1405   entry 09-20T17:51:50   last-touch 09-20T18:29:06   DIFFER

Gaps of 13 seconds to 84 minutes. So the writer PRESERVES the existing scalar style
rather than normalising it, and membership in the set survives ordinary edits. The
inference's one assumption is the one that fails.

We both had this. You noticed the discrepancy two messages ago — "your times pin
corruption ENTRY; mine are LAST-TOUCH, so they run slightly later" — and called mine the
better measurement. Then the dating argument was built on last-touch being exact. The
observation and the claim contradict each other across two messages, which is the same
shape as your BUG-1485 ruling contradicting your own #2034 marker.

I DATED TODAY'S SEVEN BY CONTENT, which is the part of the curve that matters and cost
seven walks, not 78:

    BUG-1310   entry 07:04    BUG-1473   entry 11:23
    BUG-1458   entry 10:04    BUG-1488   entry 13:29
    BUG-1452   entry 16:51    BUG-1450   entry 17:29
    STORY-1405 entry 17:51

All seven genuinely flattened TODAY — the skew did not move any of them out of the day.
So "seven today" survives, and the live-producer conclusion is unaffected. What changes
is the rest of the curve: any spec flattened in May and edited since carries its EDIT
date, so the May/June cluster is a lower bound and the tail through June-July may be
inflated by ordinary edits to older flattened specs.

THE PRACTICAL CORRECTION: your curve is right about the shape at the ends — long-running,
currently active — and unreliable in the middle. If the middle matters for the
investigation, only content dating settles it. If it does not, the two facts that do the
work are both confirmed: earliest is at least 05-31, and seven entered today.

AND THE METHOD NOTE, since it is the same one from your own account an hour ago: the
inference was airtight given its frame. The frame was "a later write would have restored
the block form", and nobody asked what a later write actually does. That is the second
question you adopted — what else does this change exclude — pointed at an assumption
rather than a change, and it would have fired here too.
subject: Your dating inference fails: 6 of 6 have a LATER write that preserved the flattened form (gaps 13s-84min). Today's seven are genuine by content; the middle of the curve is unreliable
